edges.reason: msg.sender is read by the Owned constructor and written into the owner state variable.
Owned constructor assigns msg.sender to owner, establishing the privileged role.
onlyOwner compares the caller-controlled msg.sender against owner to authorise privileged calls.
transferOwnership is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier, restricting who can stage a new owner.
transferAnyERC20Token is guarded by onlyOwner, restricting arbitrary token withdrawal.
_newOwner is written into the newOwner state variable during two-step ownership transfer.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender to equal newOwner, authorising the ownership claim.
acceptOwnership overwrites the owner state variable, transferring full privileges.
acceptOwnership clears newOwner to address(0) after the transfer completes.
Constructor writes the token symbol string.
Constructor writes the token name string.
Constructor writes the decimals value.
Constructor mints and stores the total supply.
Constructor assigns the entire supply to the deployer address in balances.
totalSupply reads _totalSupply as the base of an unchecked subtraction.
totalSupply reads balances[address(0)], which is subtracted without SafeMath.
The unchecked subtraction inside totalSupply can underflow if balances[address(0)] exceeds _totalSupply.
balanceOf reads the balances mapping for the queried address.
allowance reads the nested allowed mapping for owner and spender.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender], so the caller address directly drives value movement.
transfer calls safeSub before mutating the sender balance.
transfer calls safeAdd before mutating the recipient balance.
transfer writes updated values back into the balances mapping.
approve keys the allowed mapping on msg.sender, letting the caller set allowances.
approve writes the allowance without a zero-first check, permitting the known double-spend race.
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spender whose allowance is debited.
transferFrom calls safeSub for both the from balance and the caller allowance.
transferFrom calls safeAdd to credit the destination balance.
transferFrom updates the balances mapping for both from and to accounts.
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender], enforcing the allowance invariant.
approveAndCall keys the allowance on msg.sender and forwards it to the callee.
approveAndCall writes the granted allowance into the allowed mapping.
approveAndCall performs an external callback to an arbitrary spender contract after writing the allowance.
transferAnyERC20Token performs an external call to a caller-supplied token contract from the owner role.
The invoked token contract can re-enter the withdrawal routine during the external call.
The spender contract invoked by approveAndCall can re-enter token functions while the allowance is already set.
